subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — StellarCare next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@stellarcare.health>, Raj Patel <raj@stellarcare.health>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap — StellarCare next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared
- Consistent tail latency for customer-facing clinical summary generation (spikes during peak hours).
- Data isolation and residency requirements for PHI-associated prompts.
- Predictable unit economics: want a commitment model to reduce per-token volatility.

Goals we aligned on
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) to stabilize latency and throughput for the clinical assistant workloads.
- Private VPC peering + optional customer-managed control plane for compliance.
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime and p95 latency under 150ms for short requests (we discussed 100–200 token prompts).

Capacity proposal (initial sizing)
- Reserved cluster: 4 x A100 80GB-equivalent instances (dedicated pool) configured for 16 concurrent requests per GPU for your typical prompt mix.
- Burst pool: autoscale burst capacity up to additional 4 GPUs for seasonal peaks (billing as burst usage).
- KV/prefix cache: shared cache layer for repeated prefixes to reduce per-token compute.

Isolation and compliance
- Private VPC peering and optional Dedicated control plane (no cross-customer telemetry).
- SOC 2 / audit artifacts: attaching a SOC2-summary and sample secure config.

SLA and rollouts
- SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime with regional failover and automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model if we detect capacity constraints.
- Canary rollout for model updates with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Pricing/Procurement next steps
- Draft proposal attached (StellarCare-Dedicated-Proposal-v1.pdf) with committed monthly price for the reserved pool + burst pricing.
- Suggested internal stakeholders to loop in: procurement and security (Raj and your security lead).

Proposed next actions
1) You: confirm the sizing above (4 reserved GPUs + burst) and compliance must-haves.
2) We: send a formal SOW and Draft PO-friendly SOW doc (attached).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Dylan (infrastructure) and Logan (solutions) to finalize network and routing.

Available slots: Mon/Tue next week 10–12 PT — happy to book.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@stellarcare.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — StellarCare next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap, very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Sizing: 4 reserved GPUs sounds reasonable as a starting point. Our typical 95th-percentile traffic during business hours is ~220 requests/minute for the clinical assistant; most requests average ~120 tokens. Can Dylan confirm that the concurrency you quoted maps to that profile?
2) Data residency: we need all inference logs and model prompts retained only in our VPC in us-west-2; no telemetry leaves the VPC. Is the Dedicated control plane option you mentioned able to support that?
3) SLA: 99.95% is acceptable; we also need an escalation path and a designated SE for incidents.

Next steps for us
- I'll loop Raj (procurement) on pricing and legal.
- Please share the full SOW + SOC2 artifacts so we can start our security review.

We can do Tue 10:30 PT for the technical deep-dive — that works for our infra lead.

Thanks,

--
Alice Chen
Head of Product — Clinical Systems\StellarCare
alice.chen@stellarcare.health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Internal notes / quick engineering confirmation (copying Marissa for context):

- Concurrency mapping: 220 req/min at 95th across business hours -> ~3.7 req/s. With 4 x A100 (80GB) and our target config (16 concurrent slots per GPU), we have comfortable headroom for token-heavy requests and can keep p95 latencies ~100–140ms for 100–200 token prompts. Burst pool (additional 4 GPUs) handles traffic spikes; autoscaling policy can be set to trigger at 65% cluster utilization.
- Data residency & isolation: Dedicated control plane + private peering will ensure that inference logs remain in the customer VPC. For strict PHI controls we recommend enabling customer-managed KMS and disabling telemetry exports by default.
- Operational runbook: suggest a 24/7 on-call rotation for incidents with a named SE (we can nominate Logan or an assigned partner SE).

I'll be on the Tue 10:30 PT deep-dive and will bring a short runbook and network diagram.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
